leads.title: Tunisian Penal Code - Article 230 (1913, largely modified in 1964)
leads.documents: Criminal status of same-sex sexual activity; up to three years imprisonment for private consensual sodomy; Arabic text uses 'Liwat' (male homosexuality) and 'El Mousahaka' (female homosexuality)
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Article 230 of the Penal Code of 1913 (largely modified in 1964) decrees imprisonment of up to three years for private acts of sodomy between consenting adults.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Tunisian Penal Code - Article 226
leads.documents: Prohibition of 'outrages against public decency' used to accuse transgender people and gay people, including for cross-dressing which is not expressly illegal
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Article 226 of the national Penal Code which outlaws "outrages against public decency"'. No URL visible.

leads.title: United States Department of State - 2018 report on human rights in Tunisia
leads.documents: Enforcement of anti-sodomy law; authorities occasionally use law to detain and question persons about sexual activities and orientation
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'According to the United States Department of State's 2018 report on human rights in Tunisia, "authorities occasionally use the anti-sodomy law to detain and question persons about their sexual activities and orientation."' No URL visible.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch - March 2016 report urging decriminalisation
leads.documents: Grave abuses against gay men and men perceived homosexual including beatings, forced anal examinations, routine humiliating treatment; treatment of the 'Kairouan Six' students detained under Article 230
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'The international non-governmental organisation Human Rights Watch published a report in March 2016 urging the Tunisian Government to decriminalise consensual same-sex conduct...' informed by 'Kairouan Six'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Human Rights Watch - 6 July 2020 statement on sentencing
leads.documents: Documented incident: Tunisian court sentenced two men for homosexuality; arrested 3 June on suspicion of same-sex conduct; police attempted anal exam as evidence; related practice where refusal viewed as guilt and June 2017 case of 16-year-old sentenced to four months after refusing exam
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'On 6 July 2020, Human Rights Watch said that a Tunisian court sentenced two men for homosexuality. Police arrested the two men on the suspicion of same-sex conduct on 3 June and attempted to subject the defendants to an anal exam'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Individual Freedoms and Equality Committee (COLIBE) - Report to President Beji Caid Essebsi, 15 June 2018
leads.documents: Presidential rights machinery recommendation: outright repeal of article 230, or alternative lowering punishment to 500 dinars fine with no jail; states state and society have nothing to do with sexual life amongst adults
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'On 15 June 2018, the Individual Freedoms and Equality Committee (COLIBE), a presidential committee composed of legislators, professors and human rights advocates, recommended... decriminalization' via MP Bochra Belhaj Hmida to NBC News. No URL visible.

leads.title: Court of Appeals in Tunis - Judgement 22 December 1993
leads.documents: Transgender legal gender recognition denial; rejected trans woman request to change statut civil from male to female as 'voluntary and artificial operation' not justifying change
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'On 22 December 1993, the Court of Appeals in Tunis rejected a request from a trans woman to change her legal gender (statut civil) from male to female.' No URL visible.

leads.title: 2018 revolutionary judgement allowing trans man legal status change
leads.documents: Inconsistent recognition showing successful female-to-male legal gender change in 2018, contrast to 1993 precedent
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'However, in 2018, a trans man succeeded in changing his legal status in a revolutionary judgement.' No URL visible.

leads.title: Association Shams - enforcement statistics 2016-2019
leads.documents: Scale of enforcement post-2011 revolution: 56 jailed in 2016, 79 in 2017, 127 in 2018, at least 22 arrests as of April 2019; plus 7 Dec 2016 Sousse arrests with forced anal probe and 11 March 2017 eight-month sentences
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Local LGBTQ association Association Shams has reported that since the Tunisian revolution in 2011, an increasing number of gay men have been being jailed: 127 in 2018, in contrast to 79 in 2017, and 56 in 2016. As of April 2019, at least 22 arrests'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Habib Nouisser (2018). Sex Change in Tunisia: When Law confiscates identities - Tunisian Association for the Defense of Individual Liberties
leads.documents: Institutional report on legal treatment of sex change / transgender identity in Tunisia
leads.detail: Bibliography entry: 'Nouisser, Habib (2018). Sex Change in Tunisia: When Law confiscates identities (PDF). Tunis, Tunisia: Tunisian Association for the Defense of Individual Liberties. Archived (PDF) from the original on 30 November 2022. Retrieved 25 March 2024.' No URL visible in article text.
